subject: SR-71 Blackbird
fact: Its titanium came largely from the USSR via shell companies
detail: The CIA secretly bought Soviet titanium to build a plane meant to spy on the USSR

subject: Concorde
fact: It flew at Mach 2 and the airframe stretched about 20cm from the heat
detail: Cruising friction heated the fuselage enough to visibly lengthen it in flight

subject: Boeing 747
fact: The upper deck exists because Boeing thought jets would be replaced by SSTs
detail: The hump let the nose open for cargo once passenger 747s became obsolete (they didn't)

subject: Gimli Glider
fact: An Air Canada 767 ran out of fuel at 41000 ft and glided to a safe landing
detail: A metric conversion error left it dry mid-flight; the crew deadstick-landed on a drag strip

subject: GE90
fact: The GE90-115B fan blades are so big the engine is wider than a 737 fuselage
detail: It holds the record for highest thrust of any jet engine

subject: An-225 Mriya
fact: It had six engines and was the heaviest aircraft ever built
detail: Only one was ever completed and it was destroyed in 2022

subject: Ground effect
fact: Airliners float just before touchdown because a cushion of air forms under the wing
detail: The trapped air between wing and runway briefly increases lift

subject: Contrails
fact: Contrails are clouds made of ice crystals forming on jet exhaust
detail: They only form when the upper air is cold and humid enough

subject: Boeing 747
fact: Its wings can flex several meters at the tips in flight
detail: Wing flex is designed in so the wing absorbs turbulence loads without breaking

subject: Airbus A380
fact: It is the world's largest passenger airliner with two full decks
detail: It can carry over 850 passengers in an all-economy layout

subject: Black box
fact: Flight recorders are actually bright orange not black
detail: The orange paint makes them easier to find in wreckage

subject: Winglets
fact: Upturned wingtips cut drag and can save a few percent of fuel
detail: They weaken the wingtip vortices that waste energy

subject: Boeing 787
fact: Its fuselage is mostly carbon-fiber composite not aluminum
detail: Composites let the cabin be pressurized to a lower more comfortable altitude

subject: Auxiliary power unit
fact: The APU is a small jet engine in the tail that powers the plane on the ground
detail: It runs the lights and air conditioning before the main engines start

subject: Fly-by-wire
fact: Modern jets replace control cables with electronic flight controls
detail: Computers move the surfaces based on the pilot's inputs

subject: Cabin pressure
fact: Airliner cabins are pressurized to roughly 2400 meters of altitude
detail: That is why your ears pop on climb and descent

subject: Wake turbulence
fact: Big jets shed powerful wingtip vortices that can flip a small plane
detail: Controllers space aircraft apart to avoid this invisible hazard

subject: Pitot tube
fact: Airspeed is measured by comparing ram air to still air pressure
detail: A blocked pitot tube has caused fatal airspeed errors

subject: Boeing 737
fact: It is the best-selling jet airliner in history
detail: Thousands are in the air at any given moment worldwide

subject: Emirates
fact: It operates one of the largest A380 fleets in the world
detail: Its double-decker superjumbos are a spotter favorite

subject: Kai Tak Airport
fact: Hong Kong's old airport had a famously steep turn to land
detail: Pilots banked hard past apartment blocks on final approach

subject: Spitfire
fact: Its elliptical wing is one of the most beautiful shapes in aviation
detail: The design gave it low drag and superb handling in WWII

subject: Boeing 747
fact: The 747 earned the nickname Queen of the Skies
detail: Its hump and four engines make it instantly recognizable

subject: Concorde
fact: Only 20 Concordes were ever built
detail: Its droop nose lowered so pilots could see the runway on landing

subject: F-22 Raptor
fact: It can supercruise past Mach 1 without using afterburner
detail: Thrust vectoring lets it point its nose in extreme maneuvers

subject: Boeing 777
fact: It has some of the largest jet engines ever fitted to an airliner
detail: The GE90 fan is nearly as wide as a 737 fuselage

subject: Airbus A350
fact: Its curved wingtips and black cockpit mask make it easy to spot
detail: The composite airframe gives it a smooth quiet ride

subject: US Airways 1549
fact: Sully landed an A320 on the Hudson River after a bird strike
detail: All 155 people aboard survived the water landing in 2009

subject: British Airways 9
fact: A 747 flew through volcanic ash and all four engines quit
detail: The crew restarted the engines and landed safely in 1982

subject: Aloha Airlines 243
fact: A 737 lost part of its roof in flight in 1988
detail: The plane landed with the cabin open to the sky

subject: Chuck Yeager
fact: He first broke the sound barrier in 1947 in the Bell X-1
detail: He flew faster than sound while nursing broken ribs

subject: Wright Flyer
fact: The first powered flight in 1903 lasted about 12 seconds
detail: It covered roughly 37 meters at Kitty Hawk

subject: Amelia Earhart
fact: She was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic
detail: She vanished over the Pacific in 1937

subject: Boeing 367-80
fact: A Boeing test pilot barrel-rolled the 707 prototype over a crowd
detail: Tex Johnston rolled the jet in 1955 to show it off

subject: Concorde
fact: Its final flight in 2003 ended supersonic airline travel
detail: No airliner has carried passengers faster since

subject: Pan Am
fact: Its Boeing 707 helped launch the jet age in 1958
detail: Pan Am set the style for global air travel

subject: Airline pilot
fact: US airline captains need 1500 flight hours for the ATP certificate
detail: The rule was tightened after the Colgan Air crash

subject: First solo
fact: Tradition cuts off the back of a student's shirt after their first solo
detail: The custom dates to when instructors tugged the shirt to give commands

subject: Private pilot
fact: A US private pilot license needs at least 40 flight hours
detail: Most students actually take 60 to 70 hours to be ready

subject: Phonetic alphabet
fact: Pilots say Alpha Bravo Charlie to spell things over the radio
detail: The NATO alphabet avoids confusing similar-sounding letters

subject: Sterile cockpit
fact: Below 10000 feet crews may only talk about flying the plane
detail: The rule cuts distractions during the busiest phases of flight

subject: Checkride
fact: The practical pilot exam with an examiner is called a checkride
detail: Passing it earns the license or the new rating

subject: Type rating
fact: Pilots need a separate type rating to fly each large jet
detail: A 737 pilot cannot just jump into an A320

subject: Instrument rating
fact: An instrument rating lets pilots fly in clouds using instruments
detail: It is the single biggest skill jump after the private license

subject: Go-around
fact: A pilot who aborts a landing and climbs away is doing a go-around
detail: It is a normal safe decision and not a failure

subject: Pilot logbook
fact: Every flight a pilot makes is recorded in a logbook
detail: Hours in the logbook unlock new licenses and jobs

subject: Student pilot
fact: You can fly a plane solo at 16 in the US before you can drive alone
detail: A private license can come at 17

subject: Retirement age
fact: US airline pilots must retire at 65
detail: The age was raised from 60 in 2007
